We are looking for a Regional Retail Team Lead to join our Retail team as we scale up and drive digital and financial inclusion across our markets.

You already run a tight operation. Your counts reconcile, your people show up, your stock moves. But when did you last see a shelf you managed change what a family could afford?

Why this timing matters

M-KOPA now serves 7 million customers, up from 5 million in 2024, and has unlocked $2+ billion in credit. 86% of customers report an improved quality of life, and 55% are using a product or service for the first time. Every one of those devices sits in a shop before it reaches a customer.

If you have noticed us hiring across several roles, that is deliberate. We are building the infrastructure for the road from 5 million to 7 million to 10 million customers, and retail is where much of that infrastructure physically lives.

What makes this role different

A typical stock role: you inherit the plan, count what is on the shelf and report the variance. This role: you write the plan. You lead the Stock Controllers across a whole region, decide where inventory goes, approve corrective action when numbers drift, and shortlist the next shop location. Landlords, sales leaders, audit and finance all know your name, because you are the regional point of contact.

Why this work matters

Financial inclusion is easy to say and hard to deliver. It comes down to a customer walking into a shop and finding the right device, in stock, on the day they need it. Many of our customers use their products to earn an income, and for more than half it is their first time accessing a product or service like this. When allocation runs late, a shop closes without warning or a Stock Controller has no working tool, that customer is the one who waits. You are the person who makes sure they don’t.

Who you will work with

You report to the Retail Operations Manager and lead the Stock Controllers in your region. Day to day, you sit between the shop floor and the wider business: Area Sales Managers and Direct Sales Representatives on one side, and warehouse, audit, quality, customer service, finance and HR on the other. You also propose changes to SOPs, processes and tools based on what you see in your region, and those proposals get heard.

What you will do

  • Lead the people. Supervise, coach and develop the Stock Controllers in your region through one-on-ones, performance reviews and individual development plans, while managing shift cover, leave and workload across every outlet. You are the escalation point for people issues, the trainer who onboards new joiners, cascades every new SOP and runs refreshers and knowledge assessments, and the person who recommends promotions, performance plans or disciplinary action.

  • Own the stock. Track ageing reports and loss trends, then act before targets slip: demand-based allocation, FIFO enforcement and moving slow stock between outlets. Investigate every discrepancy to its root cause, enforce the Stock Management Policy (daily counts, reconciliation, secure storage), and report risks, trends and recommended actions, including write-offs, to the Retail Operations Manager.

  • Keep shops standing and the field supplied. Work shoulder to shoulder with Area Sales Managers and Direct Sales Representatives on allocation SLAs, outstanding devices and joint planning against sales targets, and mediate when stock and sales disagree. Manage landlords and leases so no shop faces sudden displacement, lead relocations, keep every outlet branded and audited, and run the work tools register so no Stock Controller is ever without a working tool.

What you bring

  • Demonstrable experience in retail operations, inventory or stock management, or supply chain coordination, including time leading a team. Managing people across several locations, and a background in high-volume consumer retail or fintech, will put you ahead. You motivate diverse teams, communicate clearly across functions, and handle conflict and negotiation, especially with landlords and cross-functional partners.

  • Sharp analytical and problem-solving skills: you read stock and ageing data and turn it into action. You are proficient in inventory management systems and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook), organized enough to juggle competing priorities, and driven by creative, strategic thinking and continuous improvement.

  • A Bachelor’s degree in business administration, supply chain management, logistics, retail management or a related field from a recognized university. Professional certification in inventory management (CPIM, CSCP) or project management (PMP, PRINCE2) is an added advantage.

The reality check

This role is demanding. You will cover many outlets at once, and in the same week you may be coaching a Stock Controller, negotiating with a landlord and explaining a variance to the Retail Operations Manager. When stock goes missing, you are the one who finds out why. If that sounds like the kind of problem you enjoy, you are probably ready for exactly this.

Ready to run the retail backbone behind 7 million customers? Let’s talk.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com.

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships.

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.

Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references.
